title: Mains electricity & safety
examples: What is the difference between the live and neutral wires?
Why do we use fuses in electrical circuits?
Can you explain what double insulation means for an appliance?

explain.say: Today we will learn about mains electricity safety.
The live wire carries the high electrical potential.
The neutral wire completes the circuit path safely.
The earth wire provides a safety path to the ground.
A fuse contains a metal strip that blows when current is too high.
Double insulation means two separate layers of protection.

faq.q: What is the main job of the earth wire?
faq.a: The earth wire provides a direct, safe path for excess current to flow into the ground. This prevents electric shock if the appliance casing becomes live.
asks: Why is the earth wire important?
What happens if the earth wire fails?

faq.q: Does the live wire always have the highest voltage?
faq.a: Yes, the live wire is connected to the high potential side of the supply. The neutral wire is at a much lower potential.
asks: What potential is the neutral wire at?

faq.q: How does a fuse actually protect us?
faq.a: A fuse contains a metal link designed to melt and break the circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit. This stops the flow of electricity before danger occurs.

faq.q: Is double insulation always better than single insulation?
faq.a: Double insulation provides an extra layer of protection, making it safer in case the outer layer gets damaged. It is an added safety measure.
asks: What is the benefit of two layers?
Does insulation need to be strong?

faq.q: If I touch a faulty appliance, what is the risk?
faq.a: If the appliance casing becomes live, touching it can pass a dangerous current through your body. This is why earth wires are vital for safety.
asks: What is the danger of faulty wiring?

facts: The live wire carries the high potential voltage.
The earth wire connects electrical equipment to the ground.
A fuse blows when the current exceeds its rating.
Double insulation uses two separate protective layers.

quiz.say: If an appliance overheats, which component is designed to break the circuit?
quiz.why: The fuse is specifically designed to melt and break the circuit when the current gets too high.

wrong.1: The live wire carries the dangerous current and is the source of the problem, not the solution.
wrong.2: The neutral wire completes the circuit but does not contain the safety mechanism to break the flow.
wrong.3: The earth wire provides a path away from the fault, but the fuse stops the fault at the source.

quiz.say: Which wire must always be kept separate from the live wire?
quiz.why: The earth wire is a dedicated safety connection that must remain separate from the live and neutral paths.

wrong.0: The fuse is a component that fits into the circuit; it is not a wire itself.
wrong.2: The neutral wire is necessary for the circuit to function, so it must be connected.
wrong.3: The live wire is the component that carries the high voltage and cannot be separated from the circuit.

quiz.say: If an appliance has double insulation, what does this mean?

options.show: It means the appliance is waterproof
options.say: It means the appliance is waterproof

options.show: It only works if the power is off
options.say: It only works if the power is off

quiz.why: Double insulation means there are two independent layers of insulation providing extra safety.

wrong.0: Insulation relates to electrical potential, not the voltage levels used.
wrong.1: Waterproofing relates to liquid resistance, not the electrical insulation itself.
wrong.2: The insulation is a permanent feature of the appliance design, not a temporary switch.
